q: She repeated that she has plans on that day and that she won't cancel them. […] She has an appointment for a 2 hour massage. The plan was she looks for our first one during labor but now she is out because of the massage on the same day.
cx: Second pregnancy, 2-year-old at home; her own mother drops out of minding the toddler once a birth date is set.

q: I asked my brother if he can take one day of at work, so he can take care of my daughter. I also hate to do that, I feel like I am bothering everyone, like I am asking too much.
cx: Same author, finding a back-up carer for the toddler on the birth day.

q: I dont want to be alone that day, I want my man with me but we can't have our daughter with us
cx: Same author on why the toddler plan matters: her partner must be free to be with her.

q: Usually we are a very united family and her not being supportive in this moment hurts me even more.
cx: Same author on her mother's refusal to move a massage.

q: 3 days after my due date she texted me “baby yet? <3” and while I know she meant no harm it just irritated me and I ignored it. Today, one day later, she texted me “Should I be worried? Thinking of you <3”
cx: At 40+4, a friend keeps texting her and her husband for news.

q: When the time comes we'd like to be present in the moment and not feel like we are obligated to keep everyone updated on the phone, I think this should be respected.
cx: Same author's reply to the friend; she now doesn't want the friend told when labour starts.

q: I'm already dreading when she will insist on visiting and meeting baby.
cx: Same author, past her due date.

q: Not even Braxton hicks or any hint of mucus plug here. Labor is starting to feel like a distant myth 😒
cx: Same author, 40+4, to another overdue commenter.

q: I've been looking for how women deal with physical jobs in hot environments, but every pregnant woman on here is either an office worker, a nurse, or a stay-at-home princess.
cx: Seven weeks, constant nausea, assembly-line warehouse job she can't afford to lose.

q: When we're running a line I cant just stop and run to the bathroom. I have to run at rate for 2 sometimes 3 hours straight.
cx: Same author on why desk-job advice doesn't fit.

q: I can't find any advice from women that don't have freedom during their work hours. Every post I read women are like, 'it was so hard sitting at my desk all day', or 'I just layed in bed the first 3 months'.
cx: Same author; even 'blue collar' posts turn out to be lighter jobs.

q: I just feel so defeated, I cant make this kind of money anywhere else and I need to save up for when I'm staying home with the baby. Im not single, but my husband and I cant afford for me not to work right now.
cx: Same author on why stopping isn't an option.

q: Those cooling towels they make really help with the heat. And im telling you wrap it around the back of your neck and shove the rest between your boobs.
cx: Same author three weeks later on getting through hot shifts.

q: Im at 12 weeks now. My job has been very accommodating actually. […] I just ask whoever is close to me to move pallets or carts. You just cant be shy I guess. And if I need to walk off the line my supervisor jumps in for me.
cx: Same author at 12 weeks, Pennsylvania night shift; her account of how work adapted (her understanding of state rules not quoted).

q: I feel guilty bc I’m not 100% present for my son. I feel guilty bc I’m so crabby and irritated toward my husband. I feel guilty bc my house is a disaster. I feel guilty bc I’m not prepared for baby #2. And I have zero energy to change any of those things.
cx: At 32 weeks with a 15-month-old, working full time, pregnant again unexpectedly.

q: I work full time. My husband and I alternate shifts for childcare and have a nanny one day a week. I feel like I’m losing it. I am exhausted.
cx: Same author on how the couple covers childcare.

q: I've just had to stop doing 2 of the school-nursery runs - partner not pleased - as I'm in agony with my back by the time I'm back from dropping the 3 year old off.
cx: Pregnant with twins at 27 weeks, children aged 7 and 3; no family support.

q: I'm in permenant stress from unfinished household jobs (partner does a lot but can't do it all, and we have no family support)
cx: Same author; partner works from home running a business.

q: looking back, my pregnancy with my 1st was a BREEZE in comparison. The cannot-keep-my-head-up exhaustion and all day nausea is crippling.
cx: At 9 weeks with her second, at home with a high-energy 3.5-year-old.

q: It feels like I've had the flu for the past month and I'm just so horribly non-functioning.
cx: Same author, hoping symptoms ease in a few weeks.

q: “im going to give you a reality check. most women with your symptoms dont feel better after a couple months. they tend to be nauseous until they give birth. i know thats not what you want to hear, but its better if you prepare for that.”
cx: First-time mother at 9 weeks; her primary-care doctor's words after a diagnosis of severe sickness.

q: dont wanna even tell anyone cuz they get way happier than i am and i havent even been able to think about registries and nursery themes and names and maternity photos and gender reveals and all the things that make pregnancy fun for our loved ones.
cx: Same author, too sick to enjoy or announce the pregnancy.

q: due to some issues w my insurance, i still havent seen an obgyn. i finally managed to see my pcp this week to get a referral
cx: Same author at 9 weeks, US, working part time from home.

q: sometimes I come on these sites and I see worst case scenarios of infection. Wound care, issues, months and months down the road… this is my first C-section and I’m not handling it well.
cx: Seven days after an unplanned c-section for a breech baby; nightly dread about recovery.

q: The tough part is that he works in the evening and usually comes home around 1-2 am. That means that the evening/night routine is done by myself… I also feel like children are the most neediest at night time.
cx: Ten weeks with her third, children 4 and 1.5; husband supportive but works evenings.

q: I bought some maternity pants and I already outgrew them… at 20 weeks. […] Except Amazon and nothing is actual Good quality and I can’t try it on. I bought a pair of jeans at kohls for $60- they fit for 4 months.
cx: 20 weeks in Texas at 95-100 degrees; leggings the only thing that fits.

q: My poor husband watched me try on all my clothes and he looked so sad and said “it sucks. You don’t like any of them and they don’t fit.” So now I’m on a mission to buy new stuff but it’s so much money for maternity clothes. It’s INSANE.
cx: Same author.

q: If they are comfortable they’re ugly , if they are cute they don’t feel right 😭
cx: Same author on maternity clothes.

q: I got denim shorts from Ingrid and Isabel for $20 2 pairs of work out shorts (not maternity but sized up to fit the belly) for $13 each I got 2 dresses for $13 each I got a pair of leggings (not maternity but sized up) for $13 And 5 tank tops for $7 each All of this will last me the whole summer!
cx: Same author's update after a Walmart trip.

q: I was crazy tired last time, but not this hungry. […] The other moms that I know say that they didn't experience fatigue to the extent that I am.
cx: Eight weeks with her second.

q: today my manager told me she got complaints from a dental assistant that I took two breaks this morning instead of just one. She had a whole lecture that in my downtime I need to be helping out when things are super busy.
cx: Dental hygienist, 8 months pregnant with her second, 18-month-old in a sleep regression.

q: I just think it’s completely unfair to expect the same amount of effort from someone who is a few weeks from giving birth and suffering from chronic sleep deprivation.
cx: Same author.

q: I of course burst into tears when my manger told me this because I’m tired, pregnant, and emotional, and I couldn’t stop crying all the way home. I don’t even want to go into work tomorrow.
cx: Same author.

q: My entire family lives across the country. While his parents are here and are great, I really miss my own family.
cx: End of first trimester, husband away on a week-long business trip.

q: While I’m SO excited to have this baby, I’m simultaneously mourning a life, body, and independence that I’m losing.
cx: Same author.
